report:
MRI RIGHT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Echogenic mass seen laterally in the right knee on ultrasound. Suggest for MRI evaluation.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
No prior imaging available for evaluation.

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: No definite meniscal tear, no evidence of para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intrasubstance degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is slightly laterally subluxed. Lateral trochlear inclination angle is borderline, measuring approximately 11 degrees. TT TG distance is not increased. Insall Salvati ratio is 1.4, which is also within normal range. Thickening of the lateral retinaculum may be due to prior subluxation. Increased fat attenuation is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.

Fluid

Small joint effusion is seen. No loose body. Small Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Full thickness chondral loss most observable at the lateral patella facet and apex associated subchondral chondral edema. Chondral irregularity at the trochlea is also seen associated with subchondral cysts.


Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Increasing fat signal is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.
Otherwise no focal soft tissue mass detected at the knee.

Severe chondral loss at the patellofemoral compartment particularly involving the lateral patella facet and apex associated with marked subchondral edema and subchondral cysts at both the femoral trochlea and patella. Patella is slightly laterally subluxed with borderline lateral trochlear inclination angle but normal Insall Salvati ratio and TT TG distance.

No significant knee effusion, there are no intra-articular bodies either.  
Multilocular cystic mass posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament, deep to the popliteal neurovascular bundle, in keeping with a ganglion cyst that is arising from the knee joint proper.
There is a complex, undisplaced tear through the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
There is associated high signal within the subchondral bone of the lateral aspect of the medial tibial plateau, potentially representative of a bone marrow contusion. 
Any history of direct trauma to account for such appearances?
The lateral meniscus is intact, as are the cruciate and collateral ligaments, distal iliotibial band, popliteus musculotendinous unit, extensor tendons in the remaining marrow signal throughout.
High-riding patella noted, together with pre femoral fat pad impingement - any history of anterior knee pain?
Solitary grade 3 cartilage fissure noted at the medial retropatellar facet.
Tricompartmental articular cartilage is otherwise well preserved.  
Anterior subcutaneous edema like signal change with no discrete bursal formation, kindly correlate clinically.
Grossly unremarkable remaining imaged extra-articular soft tissues. 

Impression:
Complex undisplaced medial meniscal tear.
Focal medial retropatellar cartilage damage.
Multifactorial low grade extensor mechanism pathology.
Suspected posteromedial proximal tibial bone marrow contusion.

Findings:  There is a degenerate, complex but predominantly horizontal tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. No flipped fragments and no loose bodies. Lateral meniscus is intact.  The ACL, PCL, collaterals and visualized ileo-tibial band are normal. No clinically significant intra articular effusion. No bone marrow oedema. Intact extensor mechanism.  Grade II (fissuring) chondropathy of the patellar cartilage is appreciated. Allowing for thinning of the articular cartilage of the medial femoral condyle, the remaining cartilage is well preserved.  Grossly unremarkable extra articular soft tissues.  
Impression:  Medial meniscal tear on a background of chondropathy as described above.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Sospecha lesión meniscal.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral sin alteraciones. Leve engrosamiento impresiona secuelar
del tercio proximal del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial. El resto de sus

Menisco lateral de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Rotura horizontal oblicua del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial con segmento
parcialmente desplazado hacia región intercondílea posterior. Esto se asocia discreta extrusión

Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial. El
resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones.
Leve derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo no complicado.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Discreto edema de las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Impresión:
Leve engrosamiento secuelar del tercio proximal del componente superficial del ligamento
colateral medial.
Rotura del menisco medial con segmento parcialmente desplazado hacia la región intercondílea
posterior.
Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial.
Leve derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo no complicado.
Probables fenómenos de fricción de la banda iliotibial

Findings:  There is a mild knee effusion. There is degenerate complex tearing of the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral articular cartilage is well preserved. Mild fissuring of the medial patellar facet articular cartilage is noted. Normal trochlear articular cartilage.  
Conclusion: Mild knee effusion. Complex tearing of the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus.

Constatations :

Il n’y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif au genou.

Il n’y a pas de kyste poplité. Minime liséré de liquide dans la bourse semi-membraneuse.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts. Il y a une structure ovoïde liquidienne de 0.6 x 0.4 x 0.3cm entre les ligaments croisés qui pourrait refléter une petite loculation du liquide intra-articulaire VS un petit kyste ganglionnaire (image 19, série 3).

Compartiment antérieur :

Il y a des fissure de cartilage de grade modéré à haut à la facette médiale et à la crête médiane de la rotule. Il y a aussi des changements de signal au cartilage de la facette latérale de la rotule suggérant une chondropathie débutante. Il y a des fissure de grade modéré à l’aspect inférieur de la trochlée particulièrement à son aspect central et médial. Minime quantité de liquide dans la bourse infra-patellaire profonde.

Compartiment interne :

Léger amincissement de cartilage diffus. Le ménisque interne et le ligament collatéral interne sont sans particularité.

Compartiment externe :

Légère chondropathie. Il y a des changements de signal hyperintense T2 intrasubstance à la corne antérieure/racine antérieure du ménisque latéral suggérant des changements dégénératifs. Le complexe ligamentaire latéral est sans particularité.

Conclusion :

Chondropathie modérée au compartiment antérieur et légère au compartiment interne et externe.

Il n’y a pas de kyste poplité.

Il y a un probable kyste ganglionnaire de 6mm entre les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur.
